headlines.title: 2 families displaced, dog rescued after San Jose townhome fire
headlines.description: Two families were displaced and a dog was rescued after a fire heavily damaged two townhomes in San Jose early Friday morning. Calls reporting a structure fire at the townhome complex on Bellhurst Avenue came in around 4:30 a.m. The second floor of one townhome was destroyed, and the fire spread to a neighboring unit. Two of the six townhomes in the complex were heavily damaged, while the other four were largely spared. Two families are expected to be displaced for an extended period. Residents of the four undamaged units are expected to be allowed back inside. More than 30 emergency responders were at the scene. The densely populated street created some access challenges, but officials said residents were cooperative and helped crews get the incident under control. According to the San Jose Fire Department, a dog was rescued during the fire. No injuries were reported, and the fire was under control by 5:23 a.m. The cause of the fire was not immediately known.

headlines.title: Man injured after shooting in San Jose
headlines.description: A man was taken to the hospital after a shooting in San Jose on Thursday night, the police department said. Around 8:37 p.m., officers responded to the 1800 block of Alum Rock after receiving a report that a person had been shot, according to authorities. There, police say they found a man with an injury to his head. He was taken to the hospital for treatment, officials said. The police department noted it was unable to confirm the cause of the man’s injuries as of Thursday night. Police say westbound Alum Rock Avenue at McCreery Avenue is currently closed to traffic while the incident is being investigated. Authorities encourage drivers to use alternate routes. The police department said this is an active investigation.

headlines.title: Woman will plead not guilty in killing of son-in-law at Dublin park, attorney says
headlines.description: The attorney for a Dublin woman who was charged along with her husband in the killing of their son-in-law said Thursday that she plans to plead not guilty and focus her defense on the abuse allegedly perpetrated by the victim. Shili Chen and her husband Shouyong Zhang, both 77, appeared in court briefly to ask the judge for more time before entering formal pleas. They were both charged Wednesday with murder after authorities say they both shot their son-in-law, Jonathan McKinsey, to death Saturday in a public park. The killing came days before he and the couple’s daughter were set for a hearing in a bitter divorce and custody case. Curtis Briggs, a court-appointed attorney assigned Thursday to Chen’s defense, said the court documents he has reviewed raised concerns that McKinsey was rageful and could not control his temper. “Court documents show Mr. McKinsey was extremely violent and dangerous to his family,” he said. Jennie Otis, a public defender representing Zhang, asked the judge on Thursday that he be medically evaluated, though she did not say for what. Otis declined to comment. Both required Mandarin interpreters in the courtroom. Dublin Sep 30 Dublin Sep 29 Dublin Sep 27 McKinsey, a 40-year-old gaming engineer for The New York Times, was killed in the parking lot of a sports complex in Dublin. A police sergeant was driving nearby and saw him on the ground as witnesses began calling 911 and pointing out the couple in their vehicle, who were still near the scene, Dublin Police Services said in a news release. Police detained the couple as they were driving away in the parking lot and found a gun in Chen’s possession. Prosecutors said Zhang admitted to shooting McKinsey during a later interview, and another firearm was found in the car that he admitted to using during the crime. Prosecutors also said surveillance video was recovered showing both Chen and Zhang shooting the victim. Court records show McKinsey’s killing came during a contentious divorce with his wife, Candice Jang, and a custody battle over the couple’s three young children. In petitions for restraining orders filed last year, the couple accused each other of physical, emotional and psychological abuse going back more than a decade. McKinsey, who is transgender, alleged that both Jang and her parents were verbally and physically abusive regarding a gender transition he underwent years ago. McKinsey was arrested last October and charged with misdemeanor child abuse for allegedly hitting their oldest son. Police said he acknowledged having slapped the child. Prosecutors also charged him with endangering their youngest child after deputies responded to the family’s home to talk with him and found their 2-year-old had been left home alone, according to court documents. McKinsey pleaded not guilty to the charges and alleged in court records that he had been set up by his wife, who had left the house without telling him the child was sleeping in a crib upstairs. He was released from jail on the condition that he complete 12 parenting classes. At the time of his killing, McKinsey was out on bail and had been trying to enter a mental health diversion program. It was also in October that Jang obtained a domestic violence protection order against McKinsey. Jang wrote a long list of alleged abuse by McKinsey in her filing, including an instance in 2010 when McKinsey allegedly had grabbed her by the forearms during an argument and caused her to hit the corner of a coffee table, fracturing a vertebra in her upper back. She also said that in 2023 she called the police to their home after McKinsey pushed their oldest son hard on the head. Jang also accused McKinsey of emotionally abusing her mother. The Associated Press has been unable to reach Jang for comment.

headlines.title: Chan, Wiener debate over AI and what San Francisco needs in D.C.
headlines.description: Thursday night in San Francisco, the two top candidates fighting for the California District 11 congressional seat met for a debate at the KQED headquarters. San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan faced off against State Senator Scott Wiener as they discussed everything from AI, to housing, to the future of San Francisco’s representation in Washington, D.C. The debate remained relatively calm, with both candidates getting into the specifics of their policy stances. Nancy Pelosi, who has represented the San Francisco district for the last 39 years, will retire when her current term ends. During the debate, Chan touted her support from labor groups and her focus on working-class voters. “This is the quality we need in Congress, in leadership: having that moral clarity, and having that backbone and having that courage to be able to say, ‘billionaires and corporations, pay your fair share,’ because this is our moment to make sure we can have Medicare for all, have good public education, and that we’ve got to do right for the working people across the nation,” Chan said. Wiener continued to point to his political experience, both as a supervisor in San Francisco and then as a state legislator. “We need leaders in Congress who are committed to challenging that status quo, even when it is difficult, even when there is a political cost in doing so, that is what I have done my entire time in public service,” Wiener said. Throughout the debate, the candidates’ responses touched on AI and the power of big tech companies. Chan said she would push for a moratorium on new data centers, and more federal oversight of AI development. “During the time we see it being developed, we have to have human oversight, we have to have an approval process, and that’s multiple federal agencies to be able to put that on regulation,” Chan said. Wiener noted he has been working on AI regulations in Sacramento for several years now. “I have members of Congress who call me, who ask me for feedback on policy ideas that they’re considering and introducing in Congress because I’ve been a leader on AI safety policy,” he said. Wiener also directly apologized to Chan at the debate over an AI chatbot his campaign launched (and has since ended), which Chan’s campaign has accused of producing racist and sexist responses about her. Wiener called the chatbot a “terrible mistake.” “I wasn’t looking for an apology, I was looking for, why to even start [the chatbot] in the first place,” Chan said, adding that she wants to see more regulation to curb issues like that from AI chatbots. KQED Politics correspondent Guy Marzorati emphasized that the stakes of this race remain high. “This is one out of 435 seats in Congress, but there is more importance to this one, by virtue of the fact that one of these candidates is going to be succeeding Nancy Pelosi, that is what’s hanging over this race, her legacy,” Marzorati noted. NBC Bay Area’s Alyssa Goard has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Burlingame man caught on camera tackling suspect during police chase
headlines.description: A Burlingame man was caught on camera tackling a person police were chasing after a reported robbery. It all started with a man running full speed down Lorton Avenue. Camera footage showed when he was followed by another, who quickly closed the gap and took him to the ground. The two wrestle on the sidewalk before a passing car blocks the camera’s view. The video was recorded around 12:45 p.m. on Wednesday, about 10 minutes after police received a report of a theft on Burlingame Avenue. Employees at Lululemon said two people came into the store, grabbed merchandise and ran. The robbery set off the chase that ended just a few blocks away, with an unexpected person joining in. That person asked to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation. NBC Bay Area’s Jocelyn Moran spoke with the man, who asked to remain anonymous for fear of retaliation. Watch the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: San Francisco residents concerned after apartment call boxes vandalized
headlines.description: Residents at some apartment buildings in San Francisco are concerned as call boxes have been vandalized in what appears to be an attempt to get inside. A number of apartment call boxes on Scott Street in San Francisco’s Marina District are out of service. A property owner says some of them were vandalized with water in what appears to be an attempt to get inside. Shawn, a tenant, said he moved to the area six months ago and never expected to have to worry about something like this. “We have quite a bit of packages so a little concerned if someone was tampering with it to break in,” Shawn said. On Monday, his property owner sent tenants a warning, saying the building’s call box was out of service after someone sprayed water inside, apparently trying to get through the door and steal packages. The notice also said similar vandalism had been reported around the city. Valerie lives nearby and says her surveillance camera captured a man moments before he damaged a call box with water in an apparent attempt to get inside over the weekend. SFPD confirmed a burglary was reported in the same area on Monday, at a residence where the call box had been vandalized over the weekend. Warman Security President Peter Badertscher says this isn’t new. “If the water gets in there correctly, it completes the circuit, opens the release and voilà. Bad guys in,” he said. Badertscher says his company has been dealing with this tactic for about two years and is now repairing dozens of water-damaged call boxes in San Francisco every month. He says the trick doesn’t work most of the time, but when it does, the damage can be expensive. “It’s unfortunate somebody figures out a way to circumvent the system and that bad person tells 12 more bad people and they give it a go,” Badertscher said. San Francisco police say they’re not seeing an uptick in these types of incidents citywide. In the most recent case over the weekend, no arrests have been made. For now, residents say they’re keeping a closer eye on their building entrances.

headlines.title: Pedestrian killed in Castro Valley hit-and-run collision
headlines.description: A pedestrian was fatally struck during a hit-and-run collision in Castro Valley. The incident was reported 1:29 p.m. Thursday near Somerset and Anita avenues in a residential area near Our Lady of Grace Catholic School, according to the California Highway Patrol. Alameda County Sheriff’s Office deputies have also responded with the CHP to investigate the incident. CHP said the pedestrian, a 50-year-old man, was in the roadway when struck. Police are searching for the driver and suspect vehicle. A description of the suspect was not immediately available.

headlines.title: Manny Yekutiel suspends San Francisco District 8 supervisor bid
headlines.description: San Francisco business owner Manny Yekutiel announced Thursday he is suspending his campaign for District 8 supervisor. The decision comes after the San Francisco Standard reported sexual assault allegations against Yekutiel. Supervisor Connie Chan prior to Yekutiel suspending his campaign also called for him to step down. “After a great deal of reflection, I have made the difficult decision to end my campaign for District 8 supervisor,” Yekutiel said. “I am not admitting to having assaulted anyone and some of the things that are being said about me are fundamentally untrue. But I am deeply sorry for any boundaries that I crossed. I’m going to take this time to work on myself.” Here’s the rest of Yekutiel’s statement: “As I said from the very beginning, I’m not a typical candidate. Moving through the machinery of San Francisco’s politics has left me with very little light left in my heart. This campaign has meant more to me than I can put into words. Over the past months, I have had the privilege of talking with thousands of San Franciscans about the city we love, the challenges we face, and the future we want to build together. This was never just about winning an election for me. It was about serving a city that has given me so much and bringing people together around the belief that San Francisco can once again take on big challenges with ambition, creativity, and confidence.I am incredibly proud of the campaign we built and of the community that formed around it. I am especially grateful to all of the block captains, house party hosts, family, friends, staff, volunteers, supporters, and everyone who stood with me. My campaign may be ending, but my work to help build a better San Francisco has only just begun.” The San Francisco Standard interviewed Ryan Clark, who alleged an incident happened during an SF Pride event in 2023. “Manny came up to my partner at I and touched my junk through my pants, as well as my butt. And then turned and did the same to my partner as well. He also put his hands down my partners’ pants,” he said. Clark says they both asked Yekutiel to stop, and claims they had to physically remove Yekutiel’s hands from inside his partner’s pants. The political reaction to the new allegations was swift. Mayor Daniel Lurie withdrew his endorsement, along with at least 16 other endorsements from political leaders and groups. Some stated this second allegation seemed to show a pattern of behavior they were not comfortable with. Even though Manny Yekutiel has suspended his campaign, his name will remain on the ballot because the deadline to remove his name has passed.

headlines.title: Man dies after shooting in San Francisco
headlines.description: A man died after a shooting in San Francisco Thursday afternoon, the police department said. Around 5:11 p.m., officers responded to the 1100 block of Thomas Avenue regarding a shooting, according to authorities. There, police say they found a man with an apparent gunshot wound. Officers rendered aid and the man was taken to the hospital, where he was pronounced dead, according to authorities. Authorities say this remains an open and active investigation. They asked anyone with information to call them at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 and begin the message with SFPD.

headlines.title: Unhoused group protests in front of San Jose City Hall ahead of encampment sweep
headlines.description: A group of unhoused people took their tents to San Jose City Hall on Thursday to push back against the city’s plans to clear their encampment, known as “The Jungle.” The demonstration was organized by the group Showing Up for Racial Justice (SURJ). The group said they were told on Thursday they needed to clear out by this weekend so Caltrans can clear the area. The encampment sits near Olinder Park and is considered part of what’s known as “The Jungle,” once the largest homeless encampment in the South Bay. About 45 people live in the area. “We’re trying to keep everything confined. We’re not trying to have a homeless encampment here, a homeless encampment there. No. We want to confine to one place where we’re safe enough for everyone to live amongst each other,” Jungle resident Anthony Davilla said. “Folks are anxious, upset to hear that the city is still not offering them housing and they are expected to move to nowhere, but also hopeful that the city will hear them and come to the table to truly house them and reduce homelessness like they’re saying they will,” SURJ volunteer Emma said. Mayor Matt Mahan emphasized he can’t comment on individual cases but says every resident of “The Jungle” has previously been offered alternative housing of some kind. He also says more needs to be done. “We definitely need more interim housing. We need more affordable housing. We need more mental health beds frankly but, in that case, I can tell you with confidence city teams went out there for weeks, identified every person out there, and there were exactly 121 people in that area. They were all offered interim housing. Not all of them accepted but the vast majority did,” he said. The encampment site is scheduled for abatement on Oct. 5.

headlines.title: How to detect fake content in wake of AI venomous snake hoax
headlines.description: A photo of a venomous snake in a Southern California tree shared earlier this week triggered a warning, neighborhood panic and an all-out search. It turns out it was an AI-generated image. This is far from the first time that artificial intelligence has fooled people, and it likely won’t be the last. But there are ways to protect ourselves from being fooled. First, experts suggest using your own judgement and asking yourself if an image or video seems fishy or too good to be real. If you’re still unsure, consider an AI detector. Many are free online and relatively easy to use. Detectors like GPTZero or DeepAI use pattern recognition, audio analysis and other tools to test whether content is real or fake. “Check the source that the information is from,” said Jennifer Huddleston, a senior fellow in technology policy at the Cato Institute. “Is that a source that you’re aware of? Are there other sources that are running the same image or reporting the same image?”

headlines.title: Bay Area weather forecast: Weekend heat advisory issued
headlines.description: The calendar has flipped to October, but the Bay Area will face summer-like heat this weekend. The National Weather Service has issued a heat advisory for much of the region beginning at 11 a.m. Saturday and lasting until 10 p.m. Sunday. Inland locations could see high temperatures peaking anywhere from the mid-90s to low 100s, according to the weather service. The public is encouraged to shift outdoor plans to cooler times of the day. Those who have to be outside during the hottest hours should take frequent breaks in air conditioning or shade and drink plenty of water.
